$comment: Files an UPDATE must preserve WHEN THEY ALREADY EXIST at $DEST — but still let a fresh install (or a project newly added by a later ref) create for the first time. Different from run-state-paths.json's excludes, which never touch a path at all: a blanket exclude here would also block a brand-new project's config.env from ever being extracted. These are exactly the files each project's own manifest.json declares role:"config" ("Operator-maintained declaration. Never regenerated by a run.") — see e.g. orchestrations/projects/metrolinx/manifest.json. Declared, not hardcoded in install.sh's own packaging logic: a new operator-config location needs an entry here, not a script edit.
$why: Checked 2026-09-03: JIRA_CODELINE_ROOT in a project's config.env is a per-INSTALL operator setting (e.g. pointed at a test copy of the codelines instead of the real ones) — git archive's unconditional overwrite on every --dest update would silently reset it back to whatever HEAD's committed value is, discarding that choice with no warning.
